procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (factory must be outside a free zone, with a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added).
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Prepare the certificate application including HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately; the issuing authority may request detailed cost sheets and conduct a factory visit.

Log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents (proof of factory registration, commercial invoice, and for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice), and submit the application.
Pay the certificate fee online: AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000 (fee range AED 10 to AED 200).

The certificate is issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import; it must bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority. A retrospective issuance is possible up to 12 months from shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9.

Ship the product directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information including which origin criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing, and answers a customs request within 10 working days.

Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the year of the certificate's issue; refusal to consent to a verification visit is grounds for denying preferential benefits.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Factory declared in a free zone: likely not eligible for the ministry's factory registration; confirm with the ministry.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system (unconfirmed: seen only in secondary sources).

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
